note: docs/METADATA.md 2.18 as data. 'who': both (every implementation), software (the transfer software only), builder (the device's builder, milestone N2). Hex strings are integers; byte strings are space-separated hex.

pathHash.note: /music itself; a card storing 'Music' still hashes as '/music'

qfpNote: files whose byte i is i & 0xFF
skewNote: pairs: recorded = 2026-10-07 14:30:42 + 2 days x i, observed = recorded + delta (0 when the group gives none), unless the group pins 'recorded' or 'observed' to a stamp (0, or the invalid 0x5C0773D5, month 0); 'matching' counts the pairs whose time matches under the skew. A pair with a 0 or invalid stamp is left out of the pairs (so it doesn't count towards half) and never matches, even when its two stamps are equal.

canonicalOrder.note: siblings in byte order; files in the walk's order (a folder's files before its subfolders; 'A' and its subfolders before 'A B')

fieldRules.note: a single field: the first value left after the empty ones go

names.note: 2.8.3-2.8.6: card paths from mStream's. marks: step 5's mark of a name: the FNV-1a 64 of the name as steps 2-4 left it, uncut (a file's stem, without its extension). runs: one run on a card each: its layout ('default', or the vpath layout's libraries), device.txt's extensions, what the card lists ('folder': a folder, else a file; relative to /music, as stored), and the files the run names ('bytes': original when absent, oggOpus, a conversion's format, or notAudio; 'size' 4,000,000 when absent), named in order of (server, id). names: each file's path relative to /music, in the files' order, or {'refused': why}: noName, noRoot, unlisted, tooBig, tooLong, folderFull. Made by tools/cardnames.py.

runs.note: steps 1-4 on an empty card: the vpath dropped, names made safe, the extension gated, folders past the 8th joined
a card with no device.txt: mp3 and flac only (2.15)
step 5: the file is the longest, its stem cut and marked with the stem's hash, to 255 bytes with /music/ (at a code point boundary: 254 for 3-byte characters); a tie goes to the deepest
step 5: the album folder is the longest: cut to end 64 bytes short of 255, so a sibling of 63 bytes fits whole and a longer one is cut itself
the same album first named by a long file: the folder's cut is the same
a folder still the longest name once 64 bytes short is cut again, as far as its file needs
a later run, the card listing the cut folder and no ledger row: its files join it
a folder the card has that leaves no room below it: refused, not misnamed
step 6 in one run: by match key; the lower (server, mStream id) keeps the name, the lower server first; an NFC and an NFD spelling are one name; folders merge

step 6 against what the card lists: its folders keep their spelling and merge (an NFD one too); a file named like the listener's file, a file named like a folder and a folder named like a file each take ' (2)'

the vpath layout (2.8.6): a root per library, in order of (server, vpath); the card's own folder of a root's name becomes that root; another library of the same name takes ' (2)'; the root is the first of the 8 levels
a vpath too long for a root: cut as a folder, to end 64 bytes short of 255, whatever is below

servers.note: 2.5.5, 2.6.6, 2.11: a ledger row's server. origServer: ORIG's bytes 74-79 for a row's server index. rows: the golden tags file's records in record order with their server. srvs: the golden root's SRVS entries (entry i - 1 is server i), as stored. sameServer: 2.11's test of server 'index' of the card whose root description is 'card' against what the software reads: the server at 'url' ('serverInstance': its instance, when known; 'confirmed': keys the listener has called the same server as 'url'), or, with 'peerId', that peer of it ('peerInstance': the peer's instance, when known). brokenEntries: the same test on cards whose SRVS breaks a writer rule of 2.5.5, each 'card' a root description's server fields: the entry's server is unknown, the root stays valid. The device reads neither ORIG nor SRVS.

plays.note: 2.20 and 2.5.6: the play log. slot: one play slot's fields and bytes; note: a drop note's. ids: a play's id. names: what an outcome and a source read as. atBoot: the next seq and the next bootSeq at boot from NVS's values and the card's log (the golden sync-1, or readCase's files in plays/index.json), every valid slot counting (2.20.4). deviceOps: what the device model did with log.json's events (informative). files: plays/'s files (the goldens, the reader's cases in plays/index.json). acks: ACKS's bytes, the golden root's entries, and the hardening files. resolve: a golden log through a golden tags file (the software's): each new play, sent or not (why: 'file' its file isn't a ledger row's, 'clock' no start), where to and its start; then the posted marks once the server settled the sent ones. resolveCases: single plays. peers: where a play of each row of the card of several servers goes. deviceTxt: the history key.
